problem_text: A Noetherian topological ring in which the topology is defined by an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical is called a Zariski ring. Let A be a Noetherian ring, a an ideal of A, and Â the a-adic completion of A. Prove that Â is faithfully flat over A if and only if A is a Zariski ring for the a-topology. (Lean: Module.FaithfullyFlat A (AdicCompletion I A) ↔ I ≤ Ring.jacobson A)
solution_text: Proof: Since A is Noetherian, the I-adic completion Â is flat over A (standard theorem). By the equivalence characterization, a flat module M is faithfully flat iff mM ≠ M for all maximal ideals m. So Â is faithfully flat iff mÂ ≠ Â for all maximal ideals m. Now Â/mÂ ≅ (A/m) with I-adic completion. Since A/m is a field, the image of I in A/m is either 0 (if I ⊆ m) or all of A/m (if I ⊄ m). If I ⊆ m, the completion is A/m ≠ 0. If I ⊄ m, the completion is 0. Thus mÂ ≠ Â iff I ⊆ m. Therefore Â is faithfully flat iff I ⊆ m for all maximal ideals m iff I ⊆ Jac(A), which is exactly the Zariski ring condition.
solution_summary: Use the faithfully flat equivalence (mM≠M for all maximal ideals m), analyze Â/mÂ as the I-adic completion of the field A/m, and show mÂ≠Â iff I⊆m, yielding Â faithfully flat iff I⊆Jac(A).
answer: Â is faithfully flat over A if and only if I ≤ Jacobson radical of A (i.e., A is a Zariski ring for the I-topology)
